we have obtained new results concerning the spectral analysis of operators in the context of non-harmonic Gohberg’s lemma and the non-harmonics Gershgorin’s theory.

(1) we provide a new version of Gohberg lemma, (2) we provide a non-harmonic Gershgorin Theorem, and (3) we provide sufficient conditions for the stability of solutions of a generalised version on the heat equation.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the spectral properties of non-harmonic pseudo-differential operators and the associated evolution equations, and the results are applied to the non-harmonically analysed heat equation.

we have obtained an important step in the development of the theory of non-harmonic pseudo-differential operators on manifolds, by giving a non-harmonic version of Gershgorin's Theorem, and by providing an explicit and detailed description of the spectral properties of non-harmonically pseudo-differential operators.
we obtain a non-harmonic Gershgorin's theorem, and a non-harmonics Gohberg's theorem, which are the main contributions of this paper.
, in the context of non-harmonic Gohberg’s Lemma, we have obtained an extension of some classical results of Gohberg and Gershgorine to the context of non harmonic analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have obtained a non-harmonic version of Gershgorin's theorem, and we have applied it to study the spectral theory of pseudo-differential operator in the context of boundary value problems on manifolds, as well as to study the heat equation.
we have extended to the non-harmonics setting the classical Gershgorin Theorem, Gohberg Lemma and the classical results concerning the exact domain of an elliptic operator.
we use Operator Ideales Theory and Gershgorn Theory to obtain explicit results about the spectrum of pseudo differential operators in the non harmonic analysis of boundary value operators.

the Gershgorin and the Gohberg's lemmas, and the theory of compact operators, can be used to obtain a better understanding of the non-harmomic analysis of boundary value problem.
